title: The Gilded Garden
premise: Felix Thornbury, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that fell silent a decade ago, has spent her life in the Warden's Valley, the one place where magic cannot follow and where her own strange nature goes unnoticed. When the valley's border wards collapse on the night every star in the sky goes dark, she is dragged into a war between the crown of Aldermere and the entity that has quietly worn the king as a mask for thirteen years. Guided by a disgraced court astronomer who can read the dead stars, Felix learns her silence-bound god was imprisoned by that same entity—and that her oath is the key to its cage. In the climax, she must choose between breaking her oath to free her god or keeping it to save the man she has come to love; she finds a third path, unbinding herself entirely, and shatters both the crown-thing and the old covenant. The novel ends with magic returning to the valley, Felix nameless but finally belonging to herself, and the thirteenth moon rising over an ordinary, starlit sky.
about_author: J. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping river valleys before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, divine, and personal—from a drafty house at the edge of one.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Magic
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Establishes daily life: patrol routes, the silent god's shrine, the wards she maintains without understanding them. A routine border walk reveals a hairline crack in the wardstone. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath contentment—the first hint that her invisible life is built on something fragile.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The village astrologer mentions an extra moon-turn appearing in old almanacs, a turn that 'shouldn't exist.' That night, every star goes out at once, and the border wards fall like cut strings. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as the sky she trusted simply stops.

chapters.title: What Came Through
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Things cross the fallen border—not monsters, but memories wearing shapes: people from Felix's past who never existed. She kills one and it whispers her true name, which she didn't know she had. Emotional beat: identity shaken; the valley's safety revealed as a lie she lived inside.

chapters.title: The Astronomer Who Read Ashes
chapters.summary: Isolde Vane's POV. Introduce Isolde, a disgraced court astronomer fleeing Aldermere after predicting the star-death. She stumbles into the valley seeking the last place magic cannot reach. Emotional beat: desperate hope meeting hostile suspicion; two exiles circling each other.

chapters.title: An Oath With No Voice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Under questioning, Felix admits her mercenary company swore to a god that went silent ten years ago; the oath still binds, though nothing answers. Isolde recognizes the description: the Silent One was the god of boundaries. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance formed over shared abandonment.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix leaves the valley for the first time, escorting Isolde toward the capital. The outside world is loud, magical, and wrong—stars absent, moon swollen. Bandits attack; Felix fights without her god's blessing and wins anyway. Emotional beat: disorientation giving way to unexpected competence and freedom.

chapters.title: Aldermere Under a Blind Sky
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The capital: candlelit streets, a court pretending normalcy, propaganda blaming foreign witches for the dark. Isolde risks arrest to reach her old observatory. Emotional beat: homecoming as infiltration; grief for a city that has become a stage set.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At a royal audience, Felix meets King Aldous—and sees what Isolde's instruments confirmed: something ancient sits behind the king's eyes, using him as a glove. It recognizes Felix's oath-mark and smiles. Emotional beat: cold horror; the enemy knows her before she knows it.

chapters.title: Thirteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. In the archives, Isolde uncovers the truth: thirteen years ago the king made a bargain to end a plague, and the entity—the Unmourned—took his crown, then caged the boundary-god to erase all borders, including death's. Emotional beat: revelation as vertigo; every mystery reframed.

chapters.title: The Company of the Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix tracks her old mercenary company, scattered since the god went silent. Some want to help; one, Sergeant Bray, serves the Unmourned now, believing silence meant abandonment. A knife-fight in a shrine ends with Bray's warning: 'It remembers your name because it gave it.' Emotional beat: betrayal and the ache of chosen family fracturing.

chapters.title: Moonturn Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The false thirteenth moon-turn begins; the moon visibly swells. The Unmourned's power grows nightly while the king's remaining self flickers through—a message scratched inside a gauntlet: 'Cut it out of me.' Emotional beat: ticking clock established; tenderness for the trapped king.

chapters.title: What the Stars Were For
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde deciphers that the extinguished stars were the god's prison-bars seen from outside; relighting even one requires an oath freely broken. But breaking her oath might kill Felix—or free the Unmourned instead. Emotional beat: intellectual triumph shadowed by terrible cost; growing intimacy between the women.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Following the king's clue, Felix finds a walled garden under the palace where the boundary-god's heart is buried—a living tree, leafless, guarded by Bray. Instead of fighting, Felix talks; Bray defects, showing her the root-door. Emotional beat: mercy over violence; the title's meaning revealed.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Moonlight
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The Unmourned summons Isolde, offering her stolen stars back in exchange for Felix's location. Isolde stalls, lies beautifully, and barely escapes—but it now knows they're both in the capital. Emotional beat: terror braided with defiance; the antagonist becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Name I Was Given
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Unmourned corners Felix alone and tells the truth: it named her at birth as a failsafe vessel—if the god's cage ever opens, the god will pour into her. Her whole hidden life was its design. Emotional beat: identity crisis at its nadir; she flees into the blind streets feeling like a constructed thing.

chapters.title: Belonging to Myself
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde finds Felix and refuses to let her spiral: 'A name given isn't a self decided.' Together they rework the ritual—if Felix breaks the oath not to free the god but to claim her own name, the vessel breaks and no one inherits the cage. Emotional beat: love declared plainly; despair turned to plan.

chapters.title: Storming the Gilded Court
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With Bray's defected soldiers, they assault the palace during the moon's zenith. Battles through gilded halls; Isolde holds the observatory relay; Bray falls buying time. Emotional beat: sacrifice and momentum; the cost of the climb made real.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the buried garden, Felix speaks the unbinding over the king—and chooses her third path, renouncing the given name aloud. The cage cracks; the god rises, vast and wordless, and the Unmourned erupts from the crown to seize it. Emotional beat: climax begins; selfhood asserted at the exact moment everything hangs on it.

chapters.title: Two Gods, One Grave
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The god and the Unmourned war through Felix's body, the contested vessel. Isolde anchors Felix with spoken memories—her real ones, self-made—while the king, briefly himself, drags the Unmourned back into the dying tree. Emotional beat: love as literal lifeline; the king's redemption and death.

chapters.title: When the Stars Return
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Dawn: the Unmourned is rooted, the god freed but diminished, choosing to remain as the garden itself rather than resume godhood. Stars reignite one constellation at a time across Aldermere. Emotional beat: exhausted wonder; grief for Bray and the king folded into relief.

chapters.title: The Wardstone Rewritten
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Aftermath politics: a regency, Isolde reinstated to rebuild the observatory, the valley offered a choice about its walls. Felix, nameless by law and free by choice, takes a new name of her own making. Emotional beat: quiet reconstruction; belonging redefined as chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Ends
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Coda one year later: Felix and Isolde walk the valley border together, wards now tended openly, the garden-tree budding overhead. On the final night of the thirteenth turn, the moon sets ordinary and small. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given; love and identity settled into daily life.
